title: Trusted NIP-66 monitor defaults decision
observed_behavior_before: The relay strategy plan stated the safe default for NIP-66 trusted monitors is none.
Existing user-facing and protocol docs describe NIP-66 monitor events as advisory only and explicitly configured.
Repository configuration has a trusted_relay_monitor_pubkeys field but no non-empty built-in monitor pubkey defaults were identified.
intended_behavior: Bahia ships with no trusted NIP-66 monitor pubkeys by default.
Operators may configure trusted monitor pubkeys explicitly; when configured, monitor events remain advisory health/capability metadata only.
NIP-66 monitor data cannot establish service trust, override configured trusted service pubkeys, override configured relay policy, or remove all configured relays.

rationale: No repository evidence identifies operator-approved NIP-66 monitor trust anchors suitable for development or production defaults.
The relay strategy plan and docs already define NIP-66 as configured-trust advisory metadata, never a trust root.
Shipping an empty default avoids silently inventing third-party trust anchors.
advisory_criteria_when_configured: Subscribe only to NIP-66 monitor events from explicitly configured trusted monitor pubkeys.
Use monitor events only to annotate relay health, capability warnings, or operator-facing ranking.
Ignore untrusted monitor events and events for unknown relays.
Never use monitor events to establish Bahia service trust, override trusted service pubkeys, override configured relay policy, or remove all configured relays.

included: Decision closeout for trusted NIP-66 monitor defaults
excluded: Changes to web Nostr helper modules
